_doc: THE ONE PIN of the rclone binary libs:rclone-engine ships (#567 push 4; moved here from libs:rclone by #871 move 10, so the binary is in Cloud-Lib-Rclone-Engine.apk and in no app). build.gradle reads this file, downloads each ABI's official release zip ONCE into build/, refuses on a sha256 mismatch of the zip AND of the extracted binary (the #288 / #348 fetch-once-refuse-on-mismatch pattern), reads the ELF program headers and refuses if PT_INTERP is present, and lands the binary as jniLibs/<abi>/librclone.so. That name is not decoration: on API 29+ an app may not exec a file it wrote into its own data directory (W^X), but it MAY exec what the installer extracted into nativeLibraryDir, and only files named lib*.so get extracted there — which is also why the PACKAGING APK must set packaging.jniLibs.useLegacyPackaging = true (AGP's default keeps .so files compressed inside the APK and mmaps them, extracting nothing). That APK is now Cloud-Lib-Rclone-Engine.apk: ab_cloud-libs-shared/lib-apks/build.json::lib_apks.exec_native lists this module and app/build.gradle applies it to that flavor only. RcloneExec execs applicationInfo.nativeLibraryDir + '/librclone.so' in the engine's own uid; no app execs it.
_doc_interp: WHY THE OFFICIAL linux-{arch} BUILD RUNS ON ANDROID. rclone's release binaries for linux/arm64 and linux/amd64 are Go builds with cgo disabled: measured on 2026-09-24 with a program-header walk over both binaries — NO PT_INTERP and NO PT_DYNAMIC, i.e. fully static, raw syscalls, no libc at all. Bionic vs glibc is therefore moot: nothing is dynamically linked, so the kernel runs it directly, the way Termux users run stock Go binaries. That is the property `interp: none` below declares and build.gradle re-measures on every build; a future release that links dynamically fails the build here rather than dying ENOENT on a phone. rclone publishes no android-* asset in v1.75.1 (checked via the GitHub releases API the same day), so this static linux build IS the bionic-safe choice — not a proot rootfs, which would have cost the nix-on-droid rootfs bake for one binary.
_doc_size: 78 MB (arm64) / 85 MB (amd64) uncompressed; ~28 MB in the APK (zip-compressed by AGP) and extracted once at install. The lib APK carries the ABIs build.json::android.abi_filters names.
_doc_x86_64_16k: #1881 The x86_64 binary is NOT the upstream release (4 KB-linked, fails the 16 KB page-size policy). It is built from the upstream source tag source_tag (commit source_commit) by .github/workflows/build-engines-16k.yml (CGO off, static, go linker -R=16384, every PT_LOAD p_align 0x4000 checked in that job) and published as an asset of the immutable release engines-16k-r1; url and entry override the url_template and entry_template for this ABI. arm64 stays the upstream release.
_doc_sandbox: #741 WHAT THE APP SANDBOX DOES NOT GIVE rclone, the same two gaps libs:gh's pin measured for gh (gh-binary.json::_doc_sandbox): this is a linux Go build with cgo off, so its resolver reads an /etc/resolv.conf an app does not have and asks 127.0.0.1:53, where nothing answers, and crypto/x509 finds no CA roots. RcloneExec hands every rclone child libs:sysdns's ResolverProxy as HTTPS_PROXY (the name is resolved by Android's resolver, so by whatever the SuperApp's Configs > Mesh > DNS applies) and Android's CA stores as SSL_CERT_DIR. Unlike gh, any host and any port: the remotes are the user's. idle_close_ms is 0, never cut for quiet: gh's 3s rule exists for a 6s token poll on one kept-alive connection, and on rclone it would cut a download whose server pauses mid-body; a dead kept-alive connection costs rclone a retry (--low-level-retries), not the transfer. KNOWN LIMIT: only HTTPS goes through the proxy. A plain-http remote named by host name, or an sftp/ftp remote, still has no resolver and fails its lookup (it never reaches a different DNS server); remotes named by IP are unaffected.
